items.title: Dan Barrett interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I was about 18 when I heard my first Charlie Parker record... I have a significant portion of my collection is Parker.

ctx.x: There is a concept behind that, could you elaborate on that a little bit, that is the whole concept of as a jazz musician, having to internalize time.

Yes, well it’s like a clock. You have to keep it going regardless of what’s going on around you and the best — the jazz musicians that I idolize and time recognizes, or the passage of time recognizes these people as being the best jazz musicians, and I’m thinking of Louis Armstrong and Charlie Parker, Lester Young and of course the great drummers, Jo Jones and Sid Catlett and Philly Joe Jones and John Coltrane, I don’t know, but they all, oh and Sidney Bechet, I was just listening to Sidney Bechet. He had a very…
Talk to us about playing the trombone, and how you try to impose your will over perhaps an imprecise instrument.
